state: WRITTEN all-variable candidate and disclosed symbolic auxiliary diagnostic, UNREVIEWED. No physical C/q value or source/held input used.
all_variable_result: For normal A, fix an A-eigenbasis and a common B-site basis V. If every PSD block H_i=(B+a_iI)†(B+a_iI) has offdiagonal graph a linear forest in that basis, then ρ(|H_i|)=λmax(H_i) and ρ(|H_i^[2]|)=λ1(H_i)+λ2(H_i), even if the four H_i graphs/phases differ. Each forest may be permuted and phase-gauged independently ONLY inside its scalar block-spectrum calculation; such permutations are not claimed as a common physical V. On a path, a single-particle hop cannot exchange two ordered hard-core particles, so the wedge compound is entrywise nonnegative after the path gauge. The exact cross-block decomposition then gives ρ(|K(H)|)=σ1(X)²+σ2(X)², hence η=S2. In particular B unitarily upper/lower bidiagonal guarantees this for every normal A, with generic nonnormal irreducible B allowed.
disclosed_auxiliary_diagnostic: The linear-forest hypothesis cannot be weakened to arbitrary trees by the same argument. For the all-parameter auxiliary PSD family H=tI_4+s Adj(K_{1,3}), real s≠0 and t≥sqrt(3)|s|, eigenvalues are t+sqrt(3)|s|,t,t,t−sqrt(3)|s|, so λ1+λ2=2t+sqrt(3)|s|. Its 6×6 absolute additive compound is 2t I_6+|s| Adj(C6), with spectral radius 2t+2|s|, strictly larger. This is a symbolic auxiliary PSD-family analysis, not an original physical C/q-value or a counterexample to one-normal η≤2L.
